subject: Anthropology
title: Neanderthals
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Neanderthals.

hook.text: Neanderthals buried their dead with flowers. They cared for the sick. They were not the brutes we imagined.

buildup.text: Neanderthals lived in Europe and western Asia from about 400,000 to 40,000 years ago in cold, harsh climates.

discovery.text: They had brains as large as ours, made complex tools, used fire, and hunted large game cooperatively.

twist.text: Modern non-African humans carry 1-4% Neanderthal DNA. We didn't just replace them — we interbred with them.

climax.text: Neanderthals challenge the myth of linear progress. They were smart, social, and successful for millennia.

punchline.text: They're not gone — they're part of us.

quiz.question: What does Neanderthal DNA in modern humans prove?

details.summary: Neanderthals were a closely related human species living in Europe and western Asia from about 400,000 to 40,000 years ago. They had large brains, made complex tools, buried their dead, and interbred with Homo sapiens. Modern non-African humans carry 1-4% Neanderthal DNA.
details.whyItMatters: Neanderthals challenge the idea of human uniqueness. They were intelligent, cultural beings who created art and cared for their injured. Their interbreeding with our ancestors means they are literally part of us.
takeaways: Neanderthals lived in Europe and western Asia for hundreds of thousands of years
They made complex tools, buried dead, and likely had language
Modern non-African humans carry 1 to 4 percent Neanderthal DNA

faq.question: Why did Neanderthals go extinct?
faq.answer: The exact cause is debated. Hypotheses include competition with Homo sapiens, climate change, smaller population sizes reducing genetic diversity, disease transmission from modern humans, and demographic absorption through interbreeding. Multiple factors likely combined rather than a single cause.

faq.question: Were Neanderthals less intelligent than modern humans?
faq.answer: Their brains were actually larger than ours on average. They made sophisticated tools, used fire, created art, buried their dead, and cared for injured group members. The old stereotype of Neanderthals as brutish is scientifically inaccurate — they were intelligent, adaptive humans.
